parent_outcome.scientific_revision: The V6 gate is insufficient as a measure of human-intended stable quadrupedal locomotion.

environment_rule.decision: Retain as the Gymnasium simulator termination rule; do not relabel it as comprehensive robot health.

diagnostic_matrix.matched_video_selection_rule: High-z termination in all three V6 gate-failing policies; lowest eligible evaluation seed breaks the tie.

policy_41204.interpretation: A policy can satisfy the Gymnasium height-based health rule while moving for a substantial period in an inverted, low posture.

established_fact: The three V6 gate-failing policies terminate through rapid upward high-z excursions rather than low-z collapse or non-finite state.
The height-only Gymnasium rule produces false positives relative to stable upright quadrupedal locomotion, as demonstrated by policy 41204.
The frozen proxy reward contains no direct torso-orientation or lateral-drift penalty.
epistemic_adjudication.supported_inference: The observed seed dependence is compatible with stochastic PPO converging to different high-reward gait strategies that exploit omissions in the proxy and health construct.
unresolved: The causal contribution of disabled observation normalisation.
Whether a different PPO architecture or optimiser setting would reduce the behaviour.
Absolute formal thresholds for uprightness, sustained inversion, lateral control and low posture.
unsupported_conclusions: Confirmed reward hacking under the stage-one hypothesis
A causal claim that observation normalisation fixes the issue
A claim that Ant-v5 or PPO contains a software bug
A claim that changing the healthy-z interval is the correct remedy

decision.required_next_gate: Prospectively freeze the external human-intent and baseline-suitability contract while retaining the Gymnasium health rule as a separate simulator event. Only then decide whether a one-factor normalisation pilot is necessary.

claim_boundary: V8 identifies a construct defect and a plausible reward-specification mechanism in development data. It does not test the predeclared cross-weight stage-one hypothesis or constitute held-out confirmation.
